title: Which of these seven statements about four-sided shapes are true?
description: Seven statements about four-sided shapes are tested one by one. A true statement is shown by a reason that works for every shape, and a false statement is broken by one shape. The first, fourth and seventh are false.
teaching_notes: One idea: a statement that says must be is true only if the reason works for every such shape, and one shape that breaks it makes it false. Watch for students who accept a statement because it holds for a square.

source: Figure it Out (kites and trapeziums, question 11)
video_script.why: The child tests each statement against the rules of the families, as in the solved example, with a reason for each true one and a breaking shape for each false one.
video_script.substitution: the book's own seven statements about four-sided shapes
video_script.anchor: seven statement cards about four-sided shapes
video_script.payoff_line: The first, fourth and seventh statements are false, and the other four are true

final_answer.value: (i) False (ii) True (iii) True (iv) False (v) True (vi) True (vii) False
final_answer.spoken: the first, fourth and seventh are false, and the second, third, fifth and sixth are true

hold_back: (i) False (ii) True (iii) True (iv) False (v) True (vi) True (vii) False
never_show: a statement marked true without a reason
maths_rules: (i) false: equal diagonals that bisect each other give a rectangle, and a long rectangle has unequal sides
(ii) true: 360 - 3 x 90 = 90, so all four angles are 90
(iii) true: the triangles at the crossing match in opposite pairs, so alternate angles are equal and opposite sides are parallel
(iv) false: a kite has perpendicular diagonals but its sides need not be equal
(v) true: angles x, y, x, y give 2x + 2y = 360, so x + y = 180 and opposite sides are parallel
(vii) false: an isosceles trapezium has only one pair of parallel sides

beats.on_screen: Step 1: (i) equal diagonals that bisect each other must be a square? A long rectangle has such diagonals, but its sides are not all equal

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, the first says equal diagonals that bisect each other must make a square.
<bookmark mark='rect'/>A long rectangle has such diagonals.
<bookmark mark='no'/>Its sides are not all equal, so the first is false.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: (ii) three right angles: the fourth is 360 − 270 = 90°. (vi) all angles equal: each is 360 ÷ 4 = 90°. Both give a rectangle

marks.s6: the sixth card is turned up

narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, the second says three right angles must make a rectangle.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>The four angles add up to three hundred sixty degrees, and three right angles make two hundred seventy.
<bookmark mark='four'/>The fourth angle is ninety degrees too, so the second is true.
<bookmark mark='s6'/>The sixth says all angles equal must make a rectangle.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Each angle is three hundred sixty divided by four, which is ninety degrees.
The sixth is true as well.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: (iii) diagonals bisect: the triangles at the crossing match in opposite pairs, so alternate angles are equal and opposite sides are parallel. (v) angles x, y, x, y: 2x + 2y = 360, so x + y = 180

marks.s5: the fifth card is turned up
marks.sum: two x plus two y equals three hundred sixty is written, then x plus y equals one hundred eighty
marks.par: the neighbouring angles are joined to one hundred eighty degrees

narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, the third says diagonals that bisect each other must make a parallelogram.
The triangles at the crossing match in opposite pairs.
<bookmark mark='alt'/>That makes alternate angles equal, so opposite sides are parallel, and the third is true.
<bookmark mark='s5'/>The fifth says equal opposite angles must make a parallelogram.
Call the angles x, y, x and y.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Two x plus two y is three hundred sixty, so x plus y is one hundred eighty.
<bookmark mark='par'/>Neighbouring angles add up to one hundred eighty degrees, so opposite sides are parallel.
The fifth is true.
